description: Guided vocabulary import: harvest candidate terms from where the user's proper nouns live (contacts: macOS Contacts names; calendar: macOS Calendar event titles and attendee names; github: the gh CLI's username, org members and repo names). Every source is local-first and opt-in: the preview names exactly what each source reads, unavailable sources say why, and email and Slack are not implemented (reading mail needs new OAuth scopes and reading Slack needs a workspace token; each is a conversation, not a default). Ask which sources to read first, then pass explicit sources without apply to preview candidates (at most 50 per preview, across the sources chosen). Show the candidate contents and ids; apply requires the returned previewToken and only approvedCandidateIds. Applying consumes the same snapshot without reading the sources again, once: a token is gone after one apply, after five minutes, or once 20 newer previews were made. Candidates merge like a pack install: an existing term keeps its spelling and only gains aliases; new terms are stamped import:<source> so their origin stays visible. With scope project and a project file that is not trusted yet, the file is written but left untrusted (`trusted: false`): relay `nextStep`.

apply.description: false/omitted = preview only: return availability and candidates, write nothing (default). true = write the candidates after the user approved the preview.

approvedCandidateIds.description: Only candidate ids approved by the user from that preview; required to apply, refused without apply: true; empty means import nothing.

previewToken.description: Token from the approved preview (a lowercase UUID, as the preview returned it); required to apply, refused without apply: true. Expires after five minutes or a server restart.

sources.description: Explicit sources the user approved reading. Omitted sources returns only descriptions without probing or harvesting.

name: import_vocabulary
title: Import proper nouns from the user's own sources (preview, then apply)
